newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips back on dlr buy after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips back on dlr buy after intervention.

text.p: The ringgit fell back on offshore and commercial buying of the dollar after central bank intervention helped the Malaysian unit recover from an early sell-off, dealers said.

"Dollar/ringgit is back up and is likely to try the 2.5250 level during London time," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. He said after Bank Negara's intervention, local selling interest took dollar/ringgit all the way down to 2.5210.
Bank Negara on Wednesday intervened directly, selling the dollar at 2.5250, to protect the ringgit after Thailand announced a managed float of the baht.

It was the first time in many years that Bank Negara used its own name while intervening in the foreign exchange market. It usually uses a broker or some of Malaysia's biggest banks for its market operations, dealers said.
Dealers said that up to $100 million could have been sold in defence of the ringgit during London/Sydney trading.
They said Bank Negara was expected to aggressively defend the 2.5250 level especially after rumours that a big speculator had tried to breach that level this morning.
Dollar/ringgit had tested the 2.5250 level several times in the past week.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5237/47 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5246/50 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
